text.arabic_uthmani: قَالُوا۟ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

words.gloss_range: completed plural saying by the guests as a reply and transmission channel
words.root_gloss_range: broad speech, utterance, declaration, and attribution field; here locally narrowed to reliable angelic reply that cites divine speech
words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) opens the ayah as completed plural speech, so the answer is heard as the guests' reply rather than a narrator's paraphrase. Its payoff is the conduit: many angelic transmitters answer Sārah's prior cry, yet their saying immediately yields to the singular Lord-source. The broad speech-root range is locally narrowed by that nesting, making this a reliable relay of divine attribution rather than independent angelic explanation. The repeated speech-root across the scene also makes the handoff from Sārah's speech to the guests and then to the Lord audible.

topics.headline: plural reply after Sārah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one woman's shocked speech is answered by a plural angelic group, not by anonymous narration.
topics.reason: The perfect 3mp verb carries its subject internally, and discourse continuity identifies the guests as the speakers answering the prior feminine singular speech.

topics.headline: angelic speech as conduit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the angels' saying does not stand alone; it becomes the outer frame for the Lord's cited saying.
topics.reason: The q-w-l root can be neutral about truth or attribution, but the local clause immediately embeds the Lord as source, so the surviving payoff is reliable transmission rather than the whole root range.

topics.headline: completed plural form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a completed response whose plural speaker is fused into the verb without a separate subject phrase.
topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect 3mp Form I verb; the final plural morphology supplies the group subject while the perfect presents the response as a completed narrative event.

topics.headline: speech formula develops
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same guests' speech-form has moved from greeting to authoritative confirmation.
topics.reason: The same-surah qālū recurrence is locally relevant because the guests' earlier greeting and exchange now culminate in divine attribution.

words.gloss_range: comparative preposition fused with the following demonstrative into a manner-confirmation phrase
words.prose: {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}) is small, but it begins the hinge that makes the reply work. Grammatically it governs the following demonstrative; idiomatically the two pieces act together as a manner-confirmation, so the angels first affirm 'in just that way' before naming the Lord as source. The comparison force maps the surprising decree back to what has just been announced, while the placement between two saying verbs turns the line from angelic speech into divine attribution rather than flat repetition.

topics.headline: governed but fused
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle is syntactically real as a preposition but functions with the demonstrative as one confirmation formula.
topics.reason: The bundle marks the demonstrative as governed by the kāf while translation support warns that the compound should function as a single manner or confirmation unit.

topics.headline: confirmation pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees how the reply first confirms the impossible announcement and then grounds that confirmation in divine speech.
topics.reason: The particle begins the compound placed between the outer angelic speech and the inner Lord-speech, and local reference links the phrase to the prior announcement.

topics.headline: audible fusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears that comparison and deictic confirmation are joined tightly, not staged as two separate ideas.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL sound and semantic rows converge on the particle running directly into the demonstrative while keeping both manner-comparison and exact confirmation active.

words.gloss_range: far demonstrative in the fused confirmation phrase, pointing back to the announced matter while marking a feminine singular addressee
words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكِ}} ({{tr:dhāliki}}) supplies the demonstrative center of the confirmation. It points back to the already voiced matter, especially the promised son, so the angels do not restate the whole announcement; they make the contested case itself the thing confirmed. The final feminine address marking keeps Sārah in view, and its echo with the later possessive suffix makes the response directly hers. The same confirmation formula also belongs to a miraculous-birth pattern (3:47), but locally it serves Sārah's scene and the prior announcement rather than importing the whole other passage.

topics.headline: that points to the promise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the demonstrative turns Sārah's impossible case into the very matter now being confirmed.
topics.reason: The demonstrative is discourse-dependent; contextual support points it back to the preceding announcement, while the broader options of son, announcement, or manner are narrowed to local confirmation of that matter.

topics.headline: Sārah addressed in the form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reply is grammatically addressed to Sārah, not merely spoken about her or to Ibrāhīm.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the demonstrative ending as feminine singular address, and the same addressee is confirmed by the later possessive suffix.

topics.headline: miraculous-birth formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the formulaic move from human impossibility to divine decree also seen in a birth announcement (3:47).
topics.reason: The cross-reference supports a formulaic echo with 3:47, but it is narrowed to rhetorical patterning and does not control the local referent beyond Sārah's announcement scene.

topics.headline: fronted demonstrative hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a pause on confirmation before the verb names the divine speaker.
topics.reason: The compound stands before the inner speech verb, creating a deictic pivot and cadence between the two speech clauses.

words.gloss_range: completed singular saying whose explicit following subject makes the Lord the source of the decree
words.root_gloss_range: broad saying, pronouncing, reporting, and attribution field; here selected as authoritative divine pronouncement within a quoted relay
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) is the inner saying verb, and its following subject makes the source explicit. The payoff is the shift from plural transmitters to singular authority: the angels are not reasoning from the situation but citing what the Lord said. The base active perfect form keeps that source overt and settled, while the speech-root echo with the opening word makes the chain audible. Claims about divine speech as doing are best kept as decree-force here: the local grammar proves authoritative pronouncement, not a full theology of creation-speech.

topics.headline: the Lord is the speaker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the decree is grammatically attributed to the Lord directly, not inferred by the angels.
topics.reason: The verb is 3ms and the immediately following nominative subject is the Lord-title, making source-authority syntactically explicit.

topics.headline: speech as decree warrant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reply rests on a binding divine pronouncement rather than an explanation of natural causes.
topics.reason: The Lord as subject licenses decree-force within q-w-l's pronouncement range; stronger creation-speech claims are narrowed to the local warrant supplied by divine saying.

topics.headline: plain active perfect
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the form is direct active saying, not passive rumor, ongoing deliberation, or fabricated attribution.
topics.reason: QAC marks active Form I perfect; the local wording lacks passive deagentivization or derived attribution forms.

topics.headline: singular source in speech chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same speech root move from many messengers to one source.
topics.reason: The second q-w-l verb completes the nested speech architecture and contrasts singular divine source with plural angelic transmission.

topics.headline: human speech answered
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the movement from Sārah's raw speech to ordered divine attribution.
topics.reason: The boundary rows are supported by the sequence from prior feminine speech to plural reply and then the inner divine saying.

words.gloss_range: your Lord, definite by construct with a feminine singular possessive suffix and functioning as the subject of said
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, ownership, managing, nurturing, and bringing to completion; here selected as personal Lord-source with growth resonance in the birth context
words.prose: {{ar:رَبُّكِ}} ({{tr:rabbuki}}) names the source after the saying verb and makes the decree personal: not merely a Lord in abstraction, but your Lord addressed to Sārah. The feminine suffix is a major payoff because it carries the prior speaker into the reply and keeps the reassurance directed to her. The construct form compresses definiteness, possession, and address into the title itself. The root's nurture and completion range is locally useful because the disputed promise concerns birth and growth, but it remains coloring within Lordship, not a separate claim that the word itself means pregnancy. Within the surah's Lordship thread, this is the point where cosmic and outcome authority becomes personal address, and the weighted title shifts agency away from Sārah's body to the Lord-source. The title then anchors the pronouns and the closing attributes, so the Lord who speaks is immediately identified as wise and knowing.

topics.headline: Lord as grammatical source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the Lord-title is the actor of the saying, making the decree's source syntactically direct.
topics.reason: Attachment marks the noun as subject of the inner saying verb, and the q-w-l plus r-b-b pairing is realized exactly in the local phrase.

topics.headline: your Lord to Sārah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Sārah remains the direct addressee through the feminine possessive suffix.
topics.reason: The 2fs suffix binds the Lord-title to the addressed woman and echoes the feminine demonstrative ending earlier in the phrase.

topics.headline: construct title personalization
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that definiteness and address are compressed into one construct form rather than expressed as a detached title.
topics.reason: The noun is definite by annexation to the suffix, and the bound suffix compresses possession, address, and gender.

topics.headline: growth resonance in Lordship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels why Lordship is apt in a birth scene: the title carries managing and bringing-to-completion resonance against barrenness.
topics.reason: The r-b-b family supports nurture and completion as lexical pressure, but local grammar selects the Lord-title as speaker rather than making a separate biological assertion.

topics.headline: speaker anchors the seal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks that the same Lord who speaks becomes the referent of the final wisdom and knowledge seal.
topics.reason: Cross-reference support routes the later pronouns to this subject, and the following predicates immediately characterize the same referent.

topics.headline: personal lordship within surah thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that cosmic and outcome-focused Lordship in the surah becomes personal address here.
topics.reason: Same-surah r-b-b references make the local feminine suffix distinctive: Lordship is not only cosmic or collective but directed to Sārah.

topics.headline: weighted Lord-title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the Lord-title as the weighted agency center replacing the prior focus on Sārah's body.
topics.reason: The sound observation coheres with the syntactic landing of the subject after the verb and the boundary shift from embodied reaction to divine source.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle opening the sealing nominal clause and governing the assertion through the final attributes
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) turns the reply from report into seal. After the Lord-source has been named, this particle opens a governed nominal assertion that runs to the end of the ayah: the attributes are not casual explanation but firm grounding. Its attached pronoun ties the emphasis back to the divine referent or introduces the matter with weight, and the following independent pronoun stacks that emphasis. Because there is no added emphatic lām, the assertion is strong but measured: formal reassurance rather than an oath-like escalation. The tightened opening sound also matches the boundary movement from Sārah's raw labels into a compressed formal assertion.

topics.headline: emphatic attribute seal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah shift from narrated attribution to a formal assertion of why the decree is reliable.
topics.reason: The particle opens the inna clause whose predicates are the two divine attributes, turning the second beat into standing characterization.

topics.headline: emphasis tied to referent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that emphasis is immediately fastened to the divine referent or to the matter being asserted.
topics.reason: The attached 3ms pronoun is locally coherent as reference to the Lord and also as a matter-pronoun reading; both preserve the emphatic seal without changing the predicate.

topics.headline: stacked but measured emphasis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the heavy assertion created by inna plus pronouns while also seeing that it is not intensified by an added lām.
topics.reason: The clause stacks inna, an attached pronoun, and the following separator, but the bundle explicitly notes absence of lām al-tawkīd, so the payoff is strong measured emphasis.

topics.headline: report directly grounded
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the attribute clause as the immediate ground of the Lord's saying, not a detached new statement.
topics.reason: The asyndetic transition from the speech clause into the inna clause supports a direct explanatory seal, with same-surah assertion style as a secondary echo.

topics.headline: tightened assertion sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the grammar's firm assertion reinforced by the compressed sound at the boundary from Sārah's raw labels to the formal seal.
topics.reason: The sound row coheres with the boundary movement into a highly structured emphatic clause.

words.gloss_range: independent third-person masculine pronoun functioning as a separator and emphatic subject before the predicate attributes
words.prose: {{ar:هُوَ}} ({{tr:huwa}}) is not needed just to say 'he,' because the previous word already contains a pronoun. Its payoff is separation and isolation: the subject is held in place before the attributes land, making the clause mean that He is the Wise, the Knowing. That prevents the attributes from drifting into loose description and gives the seal a restrictive force against angels, biology, or any rival explanation sharing the warrant. The address also shifts from Sārah-facing suffixes to an objective declaration about the Lord.

topics.headline: separator forces predication
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the attributes are asserted as predicates of the Lord, not left as loose descriptive apposition.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the independent pronoun as a separating pronoun between subject and predicate, and attachment places the attributes as the predicate phrase.

topics.headline: exclusive credentialing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels that the wisdom and knowledge validating the decree belong to Him, not to the messengers or natural causes.
topics.reason: The separator isolates the subject before the divine predicates, creating a qaṣr-like restriction in the local credentialing clause.

topics.headline: detached pronoun after suffix
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the repeated pronoun keeps the same divine referent present while adding force beyond reference.
topics.reason: The attached pronoun in the preceding word already supplies reference, so the independent form is meaningful as echo, separation, and emphasis.

topics.headline: attributes delayed for landing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a brief hold on the subject before the attribute pair arrives with greater weight.
topics.reason: The independent pronoun sits between the emphatic subject frame and the first predicate, delaying and acoustically preparing the attribute landing.

topics.headline: address becomes declaration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the move from direct reassurance to an objective statement about the Lord.
topics.reason: The discourse moves from second-person feminine address in the Lord-title to a third-person divine pronoun in the attribute seal.

words.gloss_range: the Wise, a definite nominative divine attribute beginning the predicate pair in the emphatic seal
words.root_gloss_range: wisdom, judgment, ruling, restraint, and making firm or precise; here selected as stable wise judgment and measured execution of the decree
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْحَكِيمُ}} ({{tr:al-ḥakīmu}}) begins the attribute landing. As a definite nominative predicate, it names the Lord not merely as wise in one respect but as the title-like Wise who grounds the decree. The root field contributes judgment, wisdom, restraint, and precision, so the impossible birth is framed as measured wise judgment rather than arbitrary interruption; derivative precision is a coloring, not a separate active form in the ayah. Because it comes before the knowledge title, wisdom leads the closing pair, making purpose and measure the first credential before the final appeal to complete knowledge. The shared cadence with the following title turns the scene from human incapacity into a formal seal, and the familiar wisdom-knowledge pairing lets this birth announcement inherit a divine-name closure also attested in 6:83, 15:25, and 43:84.

topics.headline: title-like predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees wisdom land as the predicate title of the seal, not as an object, new subject, or passing description.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment place the definite nominative attribute as the predicate of the inna clause.

topics.headline: stable intensive wisdom
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes wisdom as an enduring divine quality qualifying the decree, not a momentary act of judging.
topics.reason: The faʿīl morphology supports a stable or intensive attribute in the local divine predicate.

topics.headline: wise measured judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the impossible birth reframed as wise, judicially sound, and governed measure rather than caprice.
topics.reason: The ḥ-k-m field supports wisdom, judgment, and restraint imagery, but local form selects the divine attribute rather than activating every derivative branch.

topics.headline: precision coloring
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the decree as precise in execution, while knowing that the local word is not the Form IV verb.
topics.reason: Form IV precision and firm sound texture can color the root field, but QAC identifies the local surface as a definite faʿīl attribute, not the causative form.

topics.headline: wisdom leads knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that wisdom is paired with knowledge and placed first, so purpose and measure lead the seal.
topics.reason: The two attributes share agreement locally, and the supplied pairing evidence supports reading the first as part of a coordinated divine-name formula.

topics.headline: Lordship qualified by wisdom
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the specific birth decree generalized as an instance of the Lord's wise governance.
topics.reason: The Lord named as speaker is the referent of the predicate, and the attribute tail turns the specific report into a general divine credential.

topics.headline: wisdom begins closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the scene move from human incapacity and reaction into a paired formal seal.
topics.reason: The shared form and cadence with the following attribute support the audible closure, while boundary rows connect that closure to the shift from reaction to conceptual seal.

topics.headline: familiar divine-name closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the local birth announcement as inheriting a broader divine-credentialing pattern also attested in 6:83, 15:25, and 43:84.
topics.reason: Co-occurrence and echo rows support the broader pairing field also attested in 6:83, 15:25, and 43:84, while local adjacency supplies the actual activation.

words.gloss_range: the Knowing, a definite nominative divine attribute closing the predicate pair and the ayah
words.root_gloss_range: knowing, awareness, teaching, making known, and marking; here selected as stable encompassing divine knowledge that warrants the promised birth
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْعَلِيمُ}} ({{tr:al-ʿalīmu}}) is the final landing of the ayah. As a definite nominative faʿīl attribute, it gives knowledge title-weight and stable intensity, whether read as a second predicate or appositional partner to the preceding title. Its payoff is concrete in the scene: the Lord knows Sārah's condition, age, and the viability of the decree, so the promise is not blind assertion. The root field also lets knowing resonate with making known, fitting a scene where the impossible promise is announced while the selected title remains encompassing knowledge. It also echoes the knowledgeable son of 51:28, linking the child's described quality to the giver's encompassing knowledge without collapsing human and divine senses. The final word therefore turns the prior barrenness label into a closure on divine knowing.

topics.headline: final knowledge title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah ends on divine knowledge as its final warrant, not on the impossible birth itself.
topics.reason: The definite nominative singular attribute closes the ayah and remains tied to the same divine referent.

topics.headline: parallel or appositional partner
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that both valid parses keep knowledge joined to the same divine predicate seal.
topics.reason: Attachment allows the word as a coordinated attribute in the same predicate phrase; grammatical discussion permits either second predicate or appositional relation without detaching the referent.

topics.headline: stable encompassing knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the promise grounded in complete awareness of every condition involved, not in a bare assertion.
topics.reason: The faʿīl form presents knowledge as stable and encompassing, and the scene makes that knowledge answer the viability of the decree.

topics.headline: knowing that makes known
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a root-field resonance between knowing and making known in a scene where the promise is announced.
topics.reason: The ʿ-l-m family includes teaching and marking, but the local faʿīl divine title selects knowledge while allowing announcement-scene coloring.

topics.headline: knowledgeable son echoes source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects the knowledgeable son in 51:28 with the All-Knowing giver in 51:30 while preserving the difference between human quality and divine attribute.
topics.reason: The same root appears in the promised child's description and in the final divine title; definiteness and divine predication keep the local sense distinct.

topics.headline: paired credential cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears wisdom and knowledge as one coordinated seal, with the sequence moving from purpose to complete knowledge.
topics.reason: Local adjacency, agreement, and shared cadence bind the two faʿīl attributes into a closing pair, while the row's sequence claim is preserved as local ordering payoff.

topics.headline: knowledge seals speech of Lordship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees knowledge complete the Lord-speech configuration and generalize Sārah's case into a broader rule of divine decree.
topics.reason: The local clause contains saying, Lordship, and knowledge in one configuration, and the final attribute generalizes the specific response.

topics.headline: barrenness answered by knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the prior barrenness and incapacity label answered by the final title of divine knowledge.
topics.reason: Boundary and sound rows connect the final knowledge title to the prior impossibility language, making it the interpretive landing.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Authoritative speech restrains the impossibility inference.** `ر ب ب/B001` supplies lordship; `ح ك م/B001` restraint that sets right and B003 rightly guided knowledge; `ع ل م/B001` clear knowing. Repeated *qāla* relays the statement from Lord to messengers to hearer. I infer **authoritative knowledge -> correction of inference from bodily limits**. “Thus” reads as causal certainty grounded in who speaks.
2. **Nurture can complete what appears closed.** `ر ب ب/B002` supplies stagewise nurture/completion and `ح ك م/B004` firm perfected making. Against old age and sterility in 51:29, I infer **governing nurture -> completion beyond ordinary reproductive expectation**. This productive reading coexists with judicial wisdom.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 51:47-49 made wisdom's productive side more visible: firm making, prepared ground, and paired proportion display the same ordering knowledge asserted here.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Messenger speech is chained to formative authority.** **Lexical evidence:** repeated fixed `ق و ل/B001` is uttered speech; fixed `ر ب ب/B002` is “repair, nurture, and completion”; fixed `ح ك م/B003` is rightly guided wisdom and `B004` firm, decisive making; fixed `ع ل م/B001` is clear knowledge. **Structural cue:** reciprocal greetings, concealed provision, fear, tidings, and bodily objection precede (51:25–29); mission, criminal addressees, clay stones, marking, and extraction follow (51:31–35). **Role and abduction:** the messengers’ utterance transmits the Lord’s utterance, nurture makes the improbable birth formative rather than arbitrary, and decisive wisdom later separates rescue from punishment; I infer one knowledgeable ordering behind both outcomes. **Reading change:** “thus” reads as a transmission seal joining speech to an authority capable of completing life and discriminating judgment.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 51:31–35’s sequence of mission, marking, and extraction made wisdom visibly discriminative: the same authority that completes life also separates targets from those preserved.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi bilmek, tanımak ve onu gerçeğine uygun biçimde kavramak; böylece bilgisizlikten çıkmaktır. Haber verilmesi, öğretme, öğrenme ve bilgi bakımından üstün gelme bu çekirdekten hareket eden, belirli biçimlere bağlı kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyi bilme, tanıma ve gerçeğine uygun biçimde kavrama durumu bilgisizliğin karşıtıdır.
Bir haberin farkına varmak veya ondan haberdar olmak, bilme çekirdeğinin belirli bir konuya uygulanmasıdır.
Bildirme, öğretme ve öğrenme biçimleri bilginin bir başkasına ulaştırılması ya da kişinin onu edinmesi süreçlerini anlatır.
Karşılıklı bilgi sınamasında birini yenmek, belirli bir kuruluşta ortaya çıkan rekabetçi kullanımdır.

Bayrak, belirgin dağ, yol belirtisi, kumaş deseni ve savaş işareti gibi örnekler bu çekirdeğin farklı gerçekleşmeleridir; tanınmış kişi ve son zaman belirtisi ise benzetme veya gösterme ilişkisine bağlı uzantılardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Ayırt edici iz çıplak çekirdektir; savaşçı, kumaş, sarık ve belirli zaman göstergesiyle kurulan anlamlar kendi kuruluşlarına bağlı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi başkalarından ayıran, tanınmasını sağlayan veya ona götüren belirgin iz ya da işarettir. Bayrak, uzaktan seçilen dağ, yol belirtisi, kumaş kenarı ve sonradan konan tanıtıcı izler bu işlevin farklı gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi veya kişiyi başkalarından ayırıp tanınır kılan belirgin iz ya da işaret çekirdeği oluşturur.
Bayrak, belirgin dağ, yol belirtisi ve kumaşın kenar deseni yön bulduran veya tanıtan somut gerçekleşmelerdir.
Savaşçının, kumaşın veya sarığın ayırt edici bir işaretle donatılması belirli kuruluşlara bağlı eylemsel kullanımdır.
Tanınmış bir kişinin belirgin bir bayrağa benzetilmesi ve yaklaşan son zamanı gösteren belirti, işaret çekirdeğinin uzantılarıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar ayırt edici izi ortak temel sayar ve bayrak, yüksek ya da belirgin dağ, yol göstergesi, kumaş kenarı, kına ve sonradan yerleştirilen tanıtıcı işaretleri bu temelde toplar. Tanınmış kişi ile yaklaşan son zamanın belirtisi de görünürlük ve gösterme işlevinden doğan uzantılardır.
